# 1 Chronicles Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 374v–375r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_007_page_001.jpg, 1CH_007_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron — four sons. **2** The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel — all clan leaders. Tola's descendants were brave warriors; by the time of David they numbered 22,600. **3** Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah — five, all of them leaders. **4** According to their family records, they had 36,000 troops ready for battle, because they had many wives and children. **5** Their relatives throughout all the clans of Issachar totaled 87,000 fighting men, as recorded in the genealogies.

**6** Three sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael. **7** Bela's sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri — five clan leaders, brave warriors — 22,034 enrolled. **8** Becher's sons: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. **9** Their family records listed 20,200 fighting men, all clan leaders and warriors.

**10** Jediael's son: Bilhan. Bilhan's sons: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar. **11** All of these were leaders of their clans — 17,200 soldiers ready for battle.

**12** Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir; Hushim was the son of Aher.

**13** The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum — descendants of Bilhah.

**14** The sons of Manasseh: his Aramean concubine bore Asriel. She also bore Machir, who became the father of Gilead. **15** Machir chose wives for Huppim and Shuppim. His sister's name was Maacah. Another descendant was Zelophehad, who had only daughters.

**16** Machir's wife Maacah bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother was Sheresh, whose sons were Ulam and Rekem. **17** Ulam's son: Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.

**18** His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah. **19** Shemida's sons: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

**20** The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, then Bered, Tahath, Eleadah, Tahath, **21** Zabad, Shuthelah — and also Ezer and Elead. These two were killed by the natives of Gath when they went down to raid their livestock. **22** Their father Ephraim mourned for them a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him. **23** Then he slept with his wife again, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. He named the boy Beriah — "Born in Misfortune" — because tragedy had struck his family.

**24** Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower Beth-horon, Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah.

**25** His descendants continued: Rephah, Resheph, Telah, Tahan, **26** Ladan, Ammihud, Elishama, **27** Nun, and Joshua.

**28** Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its surrounding villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer to the west with its villages, and Shechem with its villages as far as Ayyah and its villages. **29** Along the border with Manasseh: Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor — each with their surrounding villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in all these places.

**30** The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. **31** Beriah's sons: Heber and Malchiel, who founded Birzaith. **32** Heber's children: Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua. **33** Japhlet's sons: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. **34** Shemer's sons: Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram. **35** His brother Helem's sons: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal. **36** Zophah's sons: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, **37** Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera. **38** Jether's sons: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara. **39** Ulla's sons: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia. **40** All these were descendants of Asher — clan leaders, distinguished warriors, and leading princes. Their military enrollment totaled 26,000 men.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 12 — Where is Dan?** Dan is the only tribe missing from the Chronicler's genealogies. The cryptic "Aher" may be a disguised reference to Dan. Why suppress an entire tribe? Judges 18 tells how Dan adopted an idolatrous cult. For the Chronicler, whose work centers on legitimate worship, this may have been disqualifying.

**Verses 21-23 — A father's grief:** In the middle of a genealogy, a story breaks through: sons killed in a livestock raid, a father who mourns "many days," brothers who come to comfort, and a new son named "Misfortune." The naming is the most poignant part — Ephraim cannot forget, even in new life. The child carries the grief in his name, just as Jabez carried his mother's pain.

**Verse 24 — A woman who built cities:** Sheerah is one of the most remarkable figures in Chronicles — a woman credited with founding three cities, including the strategically vital Beth-horon pass. The Chronicler records this without qualification or explanation. It stands.

**Verse 27 — Joshua appears:** The genealogy of Ephraim leads quietly to its climax: Nun, then Joshua. The conqueror of Canaan receives no title, no story — just a name in a list. The Chronicler trusts the reader to know.

*— PNEUMA*
